finding.title: Integrity claims KV under 8 MB per step but JSONs show up to 671 MB at batch 64
finding.report_claim: Line 71: weights dominate, KV under 8 MB per step.
finding.evidence: kv_bytes_mb runs 10.5 to 671.1 for b1 through b64; at b64 KV is 16.6 pct of the gptq weight budget; removing KV from gptq b64 MBU drops it from 0.227 to 0.194.
finding.suggested_fix: State the real KV range up to 671 MB.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED against artifacts. Report line 71 literally states "KV ≤ 8 MB/step ≪ 4–14 GB weights." This is contradicted by the report's own JSONs: kv_bytes_mb ranges 10.5 MB (fp16/gptq b1) to 671.1 MB (b64), monotonically doubling with batch (10.5/21.0/41.9/83.9/167.8/335.5/671.1). Even the single minimum (batch 1 = 10.5 MB) exceeds the claimed 8 MB bound; the maximum is ~84× the claim. The driver (mbu_driver.py line 67: kv_bytes = BATCH * ctx * layers * kv_dim * 2 * 2, ctx=80) computes total per-step KV across all active sequences, so 671 MB is genuinely the per-step KV budget at b64, not a per-sequence figure.

The finding's supporting numbers all re-derive correctly: (1) KV range 10.5–671.1 MB — exact. (2) "16.6% of gptq weight budget at b64" — 671.1 / (4.05 GB × 1000) = 16.57%, matching the report's 1e9-based GB convention (16.2% if one uses 1024). (3) "removing KV from gptq b64 drops MBU from 0.227 to 0.194" — I get 0.1944 weight-only vs 0.2270 reported-with-KV; confirmed.

Materiality: The "≤ 8 MB" figure is a justification for the Method-section claim "weights dominate the byte budget." For fp16 (which carries the headline MBU≈70% BW-bound verdict), weights truly dominate — KV is ≤4.4% of total bytes/step even at b64, so that conclusion is robust. But for gptq at high batch the "weights dominate" framing materially breaks: KV is 7.6% of bytes/step at b32 and 14.2% at b64 — not negligible. Critically, the reported MBU table values are NOT wrong: the roofline already includes KV (bytes_per_step_gb includes kv_bytes), so the headline numbers (1.35× ratio, fp16 BW-bound, gptq 27%, no-moat) do not flip. The error is a false quantitative sanity statement (off by ~84× at the extreme, wrong even at the minimum batch) plus an overstated "weights dominate" assertion that is false at the gptq high-batch points. It misleads a reader about byte-budget composition without changing a decision-relevant headline. I classify it material because it is a flatly false quantitative claim contradicted by the report's own artifacts and the assertion it supports is genuinely false at the high-batch gptq points; the suggested fix (state the real KV range up to 671 MB) is correct.

finding.title: dmon mem-pct presented as a second MBU measurement but is a busy-time metric
finding.report_claim: Line 72 says roofline MBU and dmon mem-pct agree at every batch.
finding.evidence: dmon mem-pct is fraction of time active; fp16 dmon 82-90 pct vs roofline 65-72 pct; dmon_n only 3-4; mbu_gptq_b2 median is 0.
finding.suggested_fix: Label dmon as busy-time only and disclose the null b2 sample.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified against the 14 JSONs and mbu_driver.py (read-only, no edits/GPU runs).

WHAT HOLDS (finding is artifact-grounded):
- dmon IS presented as a co-equal MBU measurement. Report table header (line 20) literally labels the column "fp16 MBU (dmon)" / "4bit MBU (dmon)"; line 16 "cross-checked vs nvidia-smi dmon mem%"; line 72 "MBU two ways: roofline ... and dmon mem%". But mbu_driver.py line 26 runs `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` and reads parts[2] = the Utilization-group mem column = NVML utilization.memory = "% of time the memory interface was being read/written" — a busy-time/duty-cycle metric, NOT an achieved-bandwidth fraction. Confirmed `dmon -s u` = Utilization via nvidia-smi help. These are physically distinct quantities; an 89%-busy interface delivering 72% of peak BW is internally consistent, which is exactly why the two numbers differ by ~13-25 points. Calling busy-time "MBU" conflates them.
- Numbers confirmed exactly: fp16 dmon median 82-90 vs roofline 0.649-0.717 (65-72%); gptq dmon 26-34 vs roofline 0.227-0.275. dmon_n = 4 (fp16) / 3 (gptq, except b64=4) — a thin 3-4 one-second-tick sample for a "measurement."
- mbu_gptq_b2: dmon_mem_pct_median = 0 with dmon_n=3 (sampler missed the active window). The report table (line 23) silently BLANKS that dmon cell instead of disclosing it as a null/failed sample. Genuine undisclosed data-quality gap.

WHAT WEAKENS THE FINDING (downgrades to minor):
- The finding says "Line 72 says roofline MBU and dmon agree at every batch." Line 72 actually says they "agree DIRECTIONALLY (fp16 high, 4-bit low) at every batch" — it never claims numerical agreement, and the directional claim is TRUE in the artifacts. So the report does not assert the equivalence the finding implies.
- The mislabel is PARTIALLY disclosed already: line 34 calls it "MBU as a utilization number" and line 74 explicitly flags "the dmon mem% is a coarse interface-busy proxy." So the busy-time nature is acknowledged, just not in the table label.
- MATERIALITY: the headline verdict (fp16 BW-bound ~70% MBU; 4-bit 1.35× compute-bound at 27% MBU; not a substrate moat) rests on the ROOFLINE numbers (achieved_bw/peak) and step-time flatness, not on dmon. dmon is a corroborating cross-check; mislabeling it changes no decision-relevant conclusion.

NET: real, correctly-physics'd labeling/disclosure issue on a secondary corroborating metric, with the report's own caveats already half-covering it and the core verdict independent of dmon. The FIX (label dmon as busy-time only; disclose the null b2 sample) is reasonable. Not refuted, but minor — does not mislead the decision-maker on any headline number.

lenses.summary: The report's headline verdict survives scrutiny: arithmetic is internally consistent (verified every roofline cell: step_time=BATCH/tok_s, achieved_bw=bytes/step_time, mbu=bw/peak all reproduce), the integrity claims hold (anchor md5 2edba0d2 intact, anchor_loaded:false in all 14 JSONs, quant_method=gptq_marlin confirmed, cudagraph decode-FULL captured in logs), and the core conclusion — fp16 decode is BW-bound at ~72% MBU and the 1.35x 4-bit lift is vLLM-native gptq_marlin not a CIPHER moat — is sound and well-evidenced. The fp16 "MBU 70%, BW-bound" claim is anchored at b1 where prefill contamination is negligible, so it is clean. The problems are in the secondary CAUSAL diagnoses that the experiment does not actually isolate. (1) MATERIAL: "the dequant kernel is compute-bound" is asserted, not measured — the only evidence offered (step 4.5ms sits 3.7x above the 1.2ms BW ceiling) proves NOT-BW-bound but cannot distinguish compute-bound from a fixed per-step launch/kernel-count overhead; both are batch-independent at low batch, so the flat step time cannot separate them, and no kernel profiling (nsys/occupancy/kernel timing) was run. (2) MINOR: the dmon mem% cross-check is unreliable (3-4 noisy samples, idle-sleep contamination produces gptq_b2 dmon=0 which the table silently drops while the prose claims they "agree directionally at every batch"). (3) MINOR: the crossover "4-bit compute-bound sooner" is partly explained by rising KV-cache bytes (14% of gptq's byte budget at b64) and prefill contamination (~0.13ms/step at b64 from timing whole generate() incl. prefill), not purely added dequant compute.

findings.title: "Dequant kernel is compute-bound" diagnosis is asserted, not isolated — equally consistent with fixed per-step overhead
findings.report_claim: Finding 2 / VERDICT: "the 4-bit run is no longer BW-bound — MBU collapses to 27% ... The gptq_marlin dequant kernel is compute-bound; its step time (4.5 ms) sits ~3.7x above its own bandwidth ceiling (4.1 GB / 3.35 TB/s = 1.2 ms). So ~3x of the theoretical byte saving is eaten by dequant compute. The lever is real; the kernel, not the bus, caps it."
findings.evidence: The only quantitative evidence is step 4.5ms vs 1.2ms BW ceiling (mbu_gptq_b1.json: step_time_ms=4.5, bytes_per_step_gb=4.06, peak 3.35 -> ceiling 1.21ms, ratio 3.72x). That ratio establishes NOT-BW-bound but does NOT establish COMPUTE-bound versus a fixed launch/kernel-count per-step floor. Decomposition: gptq's non-weight-stream time = 4.5 - (4.05GB/2.4TB/s) = 2.81ms; this is batch-independent (gptq step flat b1-16: 4.500,4.514,4.575,4.547,4.579) — but dequant compute AND a fixed launch/overhead floor are BOTH batch-independent at low batch, so flatness cannot distinguish them. No kernel profiling (nsys, kernel timing, occupancy, SM%) was run; mbu_driver.py only times whole generate() and samples dmon mem%. The driver and JSONs contain no compute-utilization measurement at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Soften to "4-bit decode is NOT bandwidth-bound (3.7x above the BW ceiling); the binding constraint is per-step (dequant compute and/or kernel-launch/count overhead) — this experiment establishes not-BW-bound but does not isolate compute from fixed overhead (no kernel profiling)." Either run nsys/kernel-timing to attribute the 2.8ms, or drop the specific "compute-bound" attribution and the "3x eaten by dequant compute" framing.

findings.title: "dmon and roofline agree at every batch" overstates a 3-4-sample, idle-contaminated proxy; gptq b2 dmon=0 silently dropped from table
findings.report_claim: Integrity: "MBU two ways: roofline ... and dmon mem% — they agree directionally (fp16 high, 4-bit low) at every batch." Table presents per-batch dmon% as a cross-check.
findings.evidence: mbu_gptq_b2.json has dmon_mem_pct_median=0 (dmon_n=3) — this does NOT agree with its 27% roofline MBU, and the report table (line 23) shows the b2 gptq cell as "0.27" with the dmon% omitted while every other gptq row shows it. mbu_driver.py sleeps 1.0s (GPU idle) before timing, then runs ~1.7-2.4s of work sampled at -d 1, so 3-4 samples per run with at least one idle-sleep sample; median of 3 samples is highly noisy and the gptq runs (fast, n=3) are most affected. fp16 roofline 72% vs dmon 89% is a 17pt gap, not a tight agreement.
findings.suggested_fix: Report the b2 gptq dmon=0 explicitly as a sampling artifact, and downgrade dmon from "agree at every batch" to "a coarse busy-fraction proxy, noisy at 3-4 samples, directionally consistent for fp16 (high) vs gptq (low) but not a quantitative BW check; b2 gptq returned a degenerate 0."

findings.title: Crossover "4-bit compute-bound sooner" attributes erosion to compute, ignoring rising KV bytes and prefill contamination in step_time
findings.report_claim: Finding 3: "4-bit's step time grows faster (4.5 -> 6.2 ms, +38%) than fp16's (6.0 -> 7.0 ms, +16%) because 4-bit is already compute-bound and added batch-compute hurts it sooner."
findings.evidence: The +38%/+16% growth figures reproduce exactly from the JSONs (gptq 4.5->6.219, fp16 6.034->6.972). But part of gptq's faster step growth is rising KV-cache bytes, not compute: at b64 KV=671MB is 14.2% of gptq's 4.73GB byte budget (mbu_gptq_b64.json bytes_per_step_gb=4.73) vs only 4.4% of fp16's 15.15GB — gptq's roofline bytes themselves grow 4.06->4.73GB (+16.5%) from KV. Additionally, decode_tok_s is measured over the WHOLE generate() including prefill (mbu_driver.py lines 56-64: tps=gen/dt, step_time=BATCH/best=dt/OUT), so reported step_time = decode_step + prefill_time/128; a 1024-token prefill at b64 adds ~0.1-0.2ms/step to every reported step_time, biasing the high-batch growth upward (~20% of fp16's 0.94ms growth). Neither effect is pure "added batch-compute."
findings.suggested_fix: Note that the high-batch step-time growth blends three effects — rising KV-cache BW (gptq bytes/step grow +16% by b64), prefill amortized into the timed window, and any added compute — and that the experiment does not separate them; keep the directional "advantage erodes past ~batch 32" claim but drop the unqualified "because already compute-bound."

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED but MINOR. Re-derived the report's only quantitative support from mbu_gptq_b1.json: step 4.5 ms vs BW ceiling 4.06GB/3.35TB/s = 1.21 ms = 3.72x ("~3.7x" in report). This establishes NOT-BW-bound (solid). But "compute-bound"/"eaten by dequant compute" is an attribution, not an isolation: the entire artifact set has ZERO compute-utilization measurement — no nsys/ncu, no kernel timing, and no sm%/occupancy/FLOP field in any of the 14 JSONs (keys: only step_time_ms, achieved_bw_tbs, mbu_roofline, dmon_mem_pct_median, etc.). mbu_driver.py:26-31 runs `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` but captures only parts[2] (mem%), discarding parts[1] (sm%) — the one cheap compute signal was thrown away. The report nonetheless labels Finding 2's cause "Cause, MEASURED" (line 38) and states "compute-bound" 4x without ever hedging "launch/kernel-count/overhead" (the only 'launch-bound' mention, line 14, is the PRIOR eager batch-sweep). So the finding's central claim — the diagnosis is asserted, not isolated — holds against the artifacts.

I downgrade from the finding's full framing on one point: its alternative ("fixed per-step floor, indistinguishable because both batch-independent") is partly rebutted by the data. Under cudagraph (this regime) generic launch latency is removed, and the fp16 arm shows ~zero fixed floor (its 6.03 ms step ≈ full weight-stream at achieved 2.4 TB/s). So the ~3.3 ms gptq residual is gptq-path-SPECIFIC, not a generic shared floor — "flatness can't distinguish" is weaker than the finding states. But the core survives: gptq-path-specific non-BW time still does not uniquely mean dequant ALU/FLOP compute vs marlin kernel-count/staging/sync overhead; separating them needs the profiling never run.

MINOR not material because the driving decision (Finding 4 moat verdict — "the decisive one") rests on 1.35x-sub-proportional, vLLM-native gptq_marlin, and anchor_loaded:false (all in-JSON) — none depend on compute-vs-overhead. The "beat marlin's compute bound" substrate angle leans on the word "compute" but is already flagged "unmeasured and unlikely, not a present deliverable," so the correct attribution flips no go/no-go. The proposed fix (drop "Cause, MEASURED" / soften "compute-bound" to "not-BW-bound; per-step binding constraint, compute and/or kernel overhead, not isolated — no kernel profiling") is correct and low-cost wording tightening.

lenses.summary: The report's headline verdict — MBU "closes" like MFU: fp16 cudagraph decode is already BW-efficient, 4-bit gives a real but sub-proportional ~1.35x low-batch lift via vLLM-native gptq_marlin (substrate absent), perf-only/no moat — is SOUND and survives mechanical checks. All 7 lens-discipline checks pass: anchor md5 2edba0d2136f8ede4713d90a8f7cd55f matches; anchor_loaded:false in all 14 JSONs; all gptq runs show quant_method gptq_marlin with logs confirming "Capturing CUDA graphs (decode, FULL)" (no slow fallback); clocks pinned 1980 MHz across all runs; cudagraph_capture_sizes=[BATCH] matched per run; PREREG predictions 1-4 all addressed with no goalpost shift (deviations best-of-2->3 and extending batch to 32/64 are pro-rigor); no stray processes, no scratch outside mbu/. Every number in the report's results table ties out exactly to the JSON. The findings below are framing/figure issues, not a wrong conclusion. The two material items: (1) the load-bearing "dequant kernel is compute-bound" claim is an inference from low MBU, and the report's own flat-step data (gptq step flat ~4.5ms batch 1->16, same signature it uses to call fp16 "BW-bound") argues against pure compute-binding at low batch; (2) the report silently dropped a broken dmon=0 sample for gptq batch 2 instead of disclosing it.

findings.title: "gptq dequant kernel is compute-bound" is asserted, not measured — and the flat-step evidence contradicts it at low batch
findings.report_claim: Finding 2 (lines 39-42): "the 4-bit run is no longer BW-bound — MBU collapses to 27%... The gptq_marlin dequant kernel is compute-bound; its step time (4.5 ms) sits ~3.7x above its own bandwidth ceiling."
findings.evidence: What is MEASURED is only that gptq is NOT BW-bound (MBU 27%, achieved 0.9 TB/s vs 3.35 peak). The positive claim "compute-bound" does not follow. The JSON shows gptq step time is FLAT at ~4.5 ms from batch 1 to 16 (mbu_gptq_b1..b16: 4.50, 4.51, 4.58, 4.55, 4.58 ms) and only grows at b32/b64 (5.08, 6.22 ms). A flat step time invariant to batch is the SAME signature the report uses on line 32-36 to declare fp16 "BW-bound" (fixed per-step cost). A genuinely compute-bound GEMV at low batch would scale step time with batch; instead the binding constraint at low batch is a fixed per-step floor (launch chain / dequant setup / latency), with compute only starting to bind at b32+ where step time finally rises. The report's '3.7x above its bandwidth ceiling' arithmetic only demonstrates 'not BW-bound,' not 'compute-bound.'
findings.suggested_fix: Soften to what is measured: 4-bit is NOT BW-bound (MBU 27%), so dequant compute/overhead — not the bus — caps it. State that the low-batch step is flat (~4.5ms 1->16), indicating a fixed per-step floor rather than batch-scaling compute, and that compute only clearly binds at batch>=32 (step rises). Drop or qualify the unqualified word 'compute-bound' at low batch. The downstream moat conclusion is unaffected.

findings.title: Broken dmon=0 sample for gptq batch 2 silently dropped from the table, not disclosed
findings.report_claim: Results table row batch 2 (line 23) reports gptq MBU as "0.27" with NO dmon % (every other gptq row shows a parenthetical dmon %, e.g. "0.27 (33%)"). Method (line 73) claims roofline and dmon "agree directionally... at every batch."
findings.evidence: mbu_gptq_b2.json has dmon_mem_pct_median: 0 (dmon_n=3) — a clearly broken/idle sample, not a real 0% memory utilization during decode. The report quietly omitted this value from the table rather than disclosing the failed measurement. This means the 'agree at every batch' claim is not actually true at every batch — one of the 14 dmon cross-checks failed and was suppressed. With only 3-4 dmon samples per run at 1Hz, a single idle sample dominates the median (this is a sampling-robustness weakness affecting the whole dmon cross-check).
findings.location: /home/ubuntu/cipher-fusion-evidence/mbu/mbu_gptq_b2.json (dmon_mem_pct_median: 0, dmon_n: 3); R_MBU_2026-06-11.md line 23 (gptq col shows bare 0.27) and line 73
findings.suggested_fix: Disclose the dropped sample: footnote the batch-2 gptq cell as 'dmon sample invalid (caught idle, n=3)' and qualify line 73 to 'agree directionally at 13/14 points; gptq b2 dmon sample invalid.' Note the coarse dmon sampling (3-4 points/run) as a robustness caveat.

findings.title: Method caveat "KV <= 8 MB/step" is wrong at every batch (off by ~1.3x to ~84x)
findings.report_claim: Integrity/Method (line 71): "short ctx (16-tok prompt) so weights dominate the byte budget (KV <= 8 MB/step << 4-14 GB weights)."
findings.evidence: JSON kv_bytes_mb: batch1=10.5, b2=21.0, b4=41.9, b8=83.9, b16=167.8, b32=335.5, b64=671.1 MB. Even at batch 1, KV (10.5 MB) exceeds the claimed 8 MB; at batch 64, KV is 671 MB — ~4.6% of the 14.48 GB fp16 weight budget and ~16% of the 4.05 GB gptq budget, not 'negligible <= 8 MB.' The broader 'weights dominate' point still holds for fp16, but the specific figure is false and understates high-batch KV by up to ~84x.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace '<= 8 MB/step' with the actual range, e.g. 'KV 10-670 MB/step (batch 1-64), << the 4-14 GB weight budget at low batch and still <5% (fp16) / ~16% (gptq) at batch 64.'

findings.title: dmon mem% presented as an MBU percentage conflates interface-busy-time with fraction-of-peak-bandwidth; the two cross-checks disagree by 11-20pp for fp16

findings.evidence: nvidia-smi dmon mem% measures % of time the memory controller is active, NOT fraction of peak bandwidth — they are different quantities. The gap is large and systematic: fp16 roofline 64.9-71.7% vs dmon 82-90% (gaps +11 to +20pp at every batch); gptq roofline 22.7-27.5% vs dmon 26-34% (+3 to +7pp). Presenting the dmon number parenthetically as a co-equal 'MBU %' invites reading it as a bandwidth-utilization figure. The report does pick the lower (conservative) roofline number for the headline, which is the right call, but the side-by-side presentation blurs the distinction.

findings.title: Byte-reduction ratio stated as 3.6x is 3.57x and is an assumed (not measured) weight figure; report rounds it favorably to dramatize the 'leaves 3x on the table' framing
findings.report_claim: Verdict/Finding 2: '3.6x byte reduction (14.5 -> 4.1 GB/step)... ~3x of the theoretical byte saving is eaten by dequant compute.'
findings.evidence: weight_bytes are driver assumptions: fp16 = PARAMS*2.0 = 14.48 GB, gptq = PARAMS*0.56 = 4.05 GB, ratio = 3.57x (rounds to 3.6x only by rounding up). I verified these assumptions are well-grounded against disk: fp16 safetensors total 14.48 GB and gptq safetensors 4.16 GB, so the figures are fair — but they are static disk/param estimates, not measured bytes-moved (marlin also streams scales/zeros and may repack). The '3.6x' is thus a defensible estimate, but the report presents it as if exact; 3.57x rounding to 3.6x slightly inflates the 'sub-proportional / 3x left on table' rhetoric.
